title: SKP Orchestrator
description: Orchestrator control plane -- 3 replicas across 5 queues. Six pipeline panels are shared with the processor board and generated from one source so the two cannot drift.

list.name: role
list.label: Role
list.description: Applies only to the produced / consumed / produce-duration panels -- the three instruments that carry a role attribute. See the note panel on the pipeline tier.

panels.title: Consuming
panels.description: 0 means no consumer tag on at least one queue -- nothing is listening. No other signal answers this.

panels.title: L2 gate
panels.description: The single best answer to 'why did the pipeline stop'. 0 means the gate is shut and deliveries are being requeued.

panels.title: Hydration admitted
panels.description: One-shot readiness. Separates 'not consuming because the store is down' from 'not consuming because the first hydration pass has not finished'.

panels.title: Leaders elected
panels.description: Must be exactly 1. Followers reading 0 is by design and is NOT a fault -- StepOutcomeHandler is deliberately not leader-gated, so a follower is still expected to consume. Zero means nobody holds the lease; two means a split.

panels.title: Not acked
panels.description: Deliveries the consumer refused or sent back. Drill into 'reason' on the pipeline tier for why.

panels.title: Ack lost
panels.description: The silent case: the handler ran to completion but the broker never heard the ack, so it will redeliver. Cause is on the channel-resets panel.

panels.title: Egress faults
panels.description: unroutable = the queue is not declared. transient = the broker is unreachable. Opposite remedies; this is the only signal that separates them.

panels.title: Channel resets
panels.description: Channel churn over the visible range. The cause of ack loss.

panels.title: Produced by type and outcome
panels.description: Egress. outcome != accepted is a fault.

panels.title: Consumed by type and disposition
panels.description: Ingress. Exactly one increment per delivery, on every exit path of the consumer.

panels.title: Produce duration p95 / p99
panels.description:
A real broker round-trip to publisher confirmation, not the time to write a frame.

The mean rides alongside the quantiles deliberately. It comes from sum/count and so is independent of bucket boundaries -- if it ever diverges wildly from p50, the ladder has stopped fitting the data. That is exactly how the millisecond-ladder defect was caught: p95 read 4.9s while the mean read 15ms.

panels.title: Consumer inflight by queue
panels.description: Deliveries inside a handler. PrefetchCount is 1, so a sustained 1 is saturation -- the threshold line marks it.

panels.title: Channel resets by reason
panels.description: shutdown, recovered, reopened. Each renumbers delivery tags and is what makes landed=false possible.

panels.title: Consuming by queue
panels.description:
Per-queue view of the verdict stat. A queue reading 0 while the others read 1 is one wedged consumer, not an outage.

Unfilled on purpose: the orchestrator has five queues, all sitting at 1 in health, and five filled areas stacked on one line render as a single opaque block in which a dip is invisible.

panels.title: Leader by replica
panels.description: Explains why cron fires land on one replica. Only cron fires are fenced by leadership.

panels.title: Dispatch by destination
panels.description: Per-processor fan-out from this side of the hop.

panels.title: Consumed by role
panels.description: The role attribute records what this replica was AT THE TIME it handled the delivery, so a replica carries both values across a leadership change. It is not a replica selector -- service_instance_id is.

options.content:
`role` is an attribute on **three instruments only**: `pipeline.messages.produced`, `pipeline.messages.consumed` and `pipeline.produce.duration`. Verified against the live stack.

The gauges (`gate.open`, `leader`, `hydration.admitted`, `consumer.consuming`, `consumer.inflight`) and `consumer.channel.resets` carry **no** `role`, so the filter is applied only to the four panels that can honour it. Applying it board-wide would empty the rest, because a `role=~"leader"` matcher does not match a series that has no `role` label.

The verdict tier is deliberately left unfiltered as well: it answers *is anything wrong anywhere*, and a role selection there would let a follower fault hide behind a leader view.

panels.title: Thread-pool queue length
panels.description: Explains consumption stalling while the gate is open and the consumer still reports consuming=1: callbacks are starved, not blocked.

panels.title: GC pause time
panels.description: Seconds of GC pause per second. Explains duration p99 spikes with no broker or dependency fault.

panels.title: Exception rate
panels.description: Correlates with rising parked / refused dispositions and with faulted process outcomes.

panels.title: Process restarts
panels.description: A monotonic counter going backwards means the process is new. The one signal that explains a simultaneous gap in every other series.
